```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(forcats)

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 1 & 2: Clean the Base Data (Automated + Manual Scrubbing)
# ==============================================================================
domain_long_clean <- account_by_media_domain_counts %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "author") %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -author, 
    names_to = "domain", 
    values_to = "share_count"
  ) %>%
  filter(share_count > 0) %>%
  
  # 1. Automated filter: Remove exact matches (ignoring case)
  filter(!tolower(domain) %in% politician_handles) %>%
  
  # 2. Manual filter: Catch the mismatched handles and non-media blogs
  filter(!domain %in% c("lpbraganca", "pedrolupion", "sandersonfederal", "gurgelrj", 
                        "marcelvanhattem", "franciscojr", "deputadohugoleal", "evairdemelo", 
                        "charliesevangelista", "christinoaureo", "jaquelinecassol", 
                        "osiresdamaso", "renataabreuoficial", "domingossavio", "leandre", 
                        "joaoroma", "nereucrispim", "prb10", "agriculturarsgovbr",
                        "portaltanosite", "blogdomarcosjunior", "gdia"))

# ==============================================================================
# Re-run the rest of the pipeline to generate the plot
# ==============================================================================
right_shares_clean <- domain_long_clean %>%
  inner_join(right_nodes %>% select(author, is_wolf), by = "author")

domain_signatures_clean <- right_shares_clean %>%
  group_by(is_wolf, domain) %>%
  summarise(shares = sum(share_count, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = is_wolf, values_from = shares, values_fill = 0, names_prefix = "wolf_") %>%
  rename(non_wolf_shares = wolf_0, wolf_shares = wolf_1) %>%
  mutate(
    total_non_wolf = sum(non_wolf_shares),
    total_wolf = sum(wolf_shares),
    rate_non_wolf = (non_wolf_shares + 1) / (total_non_wolf + 1),
    rate_wolf = (wolf_shares + 1) / (total_wolf + 1),
    log_odds_ratio = log(rate_wolf / rate_non_wolf),
    total_shares = wolf_shares + non_wolf_shares
  ) %>%
  filter(total_shares >= 20)

top_distinctive_clean <- domain_signatures_clean %>%
  group_by(log_odds_ratio > 0) %>%
  slice_max(abs(log_odds_ratio), n = 15) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    faction = ifelse(log_odds_ratio > 0, "Distinctly Wolf", "Distinctly Non-Wolf"),
    domain = fct_reorder(domain, log_odds_ratio)
  )

ggplot(top_distinctive_clean, aes(x = log_odds_ratio, y = domain, fill = faction)) +
  geom_col(alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(wolf_shares, " / ", non_wolf_shares), hjust = ifelse(log_odds_ratio > 0, -0.1, 1.1)), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Distinctly Wolf" = "darkred", "Distinctly Non-Wolf" = "steelblue")) +
  expand_limits(x = c(min(top_distinctive_clean$log_odds_ratio) * 1.3, max(top_distinctive_clean$log_odds_ratio) * 1.3)) +
  labs(
    title = "Differential Media Signatures: Wolves vs. Non-Wolves (Cleaned)",
    subtitle = "Excludes intra-parliamentary retweets/shares. Labels = Absolute Shares.",
    x = "Log Odds Ratio (< 0: Non-Wolf | > 0: Wolf)",
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Faction Signature"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 1: Calculate Total Media Output (The Denominators)
# ==============================================================================
group_budgets <- right_shares_clean %>%
  group_by(is_wolf) %>%
  summarise(total_faction_shares = sum(share_count), .groups = "drop")

total_w_shares <- group_budgets %>% filter(is_wolf == 1) %>% pull(total_faction_shares)
total_nw_shares <- group_budgets %>% filter(is_wolf == 0) %>% pull(total_faction_shares)

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 2: Compute Attention Share per Domain
# ==============================================================================
media_diet_shares <- right_shares_clean %>%
  group_by(is_wolf, domain) %>%
  summarise(domain_faction_shares = sum(share_count), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = is_wolf, 
    values_from = domain_faction_shares, 
    values_fill = 0, 
    names_prefix = "shares_"
  ) %>%
  rename(nw_shares = shares_0, w_shares = shares_1) %>%
  mutate(
    # What % of their total media diet does each group give to this domain?
    pct_of_wolf_diet = (w_shares / total_w_shares) * 100,
    pct_of_nonwolf_diet = (nw_shares / total_nw_shares) * 100,
    
    total_volume = w_shares + nw_shares,
    
    # Calculate an asymmetric ratio for labeling decisions
    diet_ratio = (pct_of_wolf_diet + 0.001) / (pct_of_nonwolf_diet + 0.001)
  ) %>%
  # Keep domains with a minimum baseline of overall shares to avoid tiny noise
  filter(total_volume >= 20)

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 3: Plot the Media Diet Space
# ==============================================================================
ggplot(media_diet_shares, aes(x = pct_of_nonwolf_diet, y = pct_of_wolf_diet)) +
  
  # 45-degree identity line: Domains on this line get EQUAL attention from both groups
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  
  # Plot domains as points, sized by their total volume
  geom_point(aes(size = total_volume), color = "purple4", alpha = 0.6) +
  
  # Log scales are necessary because a few domains (like globo/exame) take massive chunks of the diet
  scale_x_log10(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  
  # Label the most distinct outliers on both sides
  geom_text_repel(
    data = media_diet_shares %>% filter(diet_ratio > 3.5 | diet_ratio < 0.25 | total_volume > 2000),
    aes(label = domain),
    size = 3.5,
    box.padding = 0.4,
    max.overlaps = 20
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "The Right-Wing Media Diet Space",
    subtitle = "Compares the percentage of each faction's total link budget dedicated to a given domain.",
    x = "Share of Non-Wolf Media Diet (Log Scale)",
    y = "Share of Wolf Media Diet (Log Scale)",
    size = "Total Combined Shares"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 1: Calculate Diet Attention Shares
# ==============================================================================
group_budgets <- right_shares_clean %>%
  group_by(is_wolf) %>%
  summarise(total_faction_shares = sum(share_count), .groups = "drop")

total_w_shares <- group_budgets %>% filter(is_wolf == 1) %>% pull(total_faction_shares)
total_nw_shares <- group_budgets %>% filter(is_wolf == 0) %>% pull(total_faction_shares)

media_diet_base <- right_shares_clean %>%
  group_by(is_wolf, domain) %>%
  summarise(domain_faction_shares = sum(share_count), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = is_wolf, values_from = domain_faction_shares, values_fill = 0, names_prefix = "shares_") %>%
  rename(nw_shares = shares_0, w_shares = shares_1) %>%
  mutate(
    pct_of_wolf_diet = (w_shares / total_w_shares) * 100,
    pct_of_nonwolf_diet = (nw_shares / total_nw_shares) * 100,
    total_volume = w_shares + nw_shares,
    diet_ratio = (pct_of_wolf_diet + 0.001) / (pct_of_nonwolf_diet + 0.001)
  ) %>%
  filter(total_volume >= 20)

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 2: Inject Domain-Level Ideology and Exclusivity Metadata (CORRECTED)
# ==============================================================================
media_diet_enriched <- media_diet_base %>%
  left_join(
    domain_ideology_summary %>% 
      select(domain, weighted_mean_ideology, weighted_sd_ideology),
    by = "domain"
  )

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 3: Plot with Ideological/Exclusivity Color Coding
# ==============================================================================
ggplot(media_diet_enriched, aes(x = pct_of_nonwolf_diet, y = pct_of_wolf_diet)) +
  
  # 45-degree identity line (Equal attention)
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray60") +
  
  # Color points by domain ideology (Blue = Left/Center, Red = Right)
  # Alpha (transparency) is linked to Exclusivity: Lower SD = Higher Exclusivity = More Opaque
  geom_point(aes(color = weighted_mean_ideology, size = total_volume, alpha = 1 - weighted_sd_ideology)) +
  
  # Log scales to handle the massive distribution gap
  scale_x_log10(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  
  # Continuous color scale centered at 0 (neutral/center baseline)
  scale_color_gradient2(
    low = "steelblue", 
    mid = "gray90", 
    high = "darkred", 
    midpoint = 0,
    name = "Domain Ideology\nScore"
  ) +
  
  # Guide for visibility adjustments
  scale_alpha_continuous(name = "Domain Exclusivity\n(1 - SD)", range = c(0.4, 1)) +
  scale_size_continuous(name = "Total Combined Shares", labels = scales::comma) +
  
  # Label the critical diagnostic anchors
  geom_text_repel(
    data = media_diet_enriched %>% filter(diet_ratio > 3.5 | diet_ratio < 0.25 | total_volume > 2000),
    aes(label = domain),
    size = 3.5,
    box.padding = 0.4,
    max.overlaps = 25
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "The Ideological Geography of the Right-Wing Media Diet",
    subtitle = "Color maps the underlying domain ideology; transparency highlights echo-chamber exclusivity.",
    x = "Share of Non-Wolf Media Diet (Log Scale)",
    y = "Share of Wolf Media Diet (Log Scale)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
```



```{r domain ideology}
# 1. Convert the wide matrix into a long dataframe
domain_long <- account_by_media_domain_counts %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  # Move the row names (the account handles) into a proper column
  rownames_to_column(var = "author") %>%
  # Pivot all domain columns into two columns: 'domain' and 'share_count'
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -author, 
    names_to = "domain", 
    values_to = "share_count"
  ) %>%
  # Filter out the zeroes immediately to save memory and processing time
  filter(share_count > 0)

# 2. Merge with legislator data and calculate ideological metrics
domain_ideology_summary <- domain_long %>%
  # Join only the necessary columns from nodes_breakdown
  inner_join(
    nodes_breakdown %>% select(author, party, ideology_2021), 
    by = "author"
  ) %>%
  group_by(domain) %>%
  summarise(
    total_shares = sum(share_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    # Weighted Mean
    weighted_mean_ideology = sum(share_count * ideology_2021, na.rm = TRUE) / total_shares,
    
    # Weighted Variance and Standard Deviation
    weighted_variance = sum(share_count * (ideology_2021 - weighted_mean_ideology)^2, na.rm = TRUE) / total_shares,
    weighted_sd_ideology = sqrt(weighted_variance),
    
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Filter out low-frequency domains to avoid artificial 0 standard deviations
  filter(total_shares >= 10) %>%
  # Sort by total shares descending for readability
  arrange(desc(total_shares))
```


```{r domain compass, echo=FALSE}
ggplot(domain_ideology_summary, aes(x = weighted_mean_ideology, y = total_shares)) +
  
  # 1. Plot the points. Color maps to the standard deviation (exclusivity)
  geom_point(aes(color = weighted_sd_ideology), alpha = 0.7, size = 2.5) +
  
  # 2. Use a log10 scale for the Y-axis to handle power-law frequency distributions
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
  
  # 3. Add a vertical line at 0 to denote the ideological center
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  
  # 4. Label only the top 5% most shared domains to prevent unreadable text overlap
  geom_text_repel(
    data = subset(domain_ideology_summary, total_shares > quantile(total_shares, 0.95)),
    aes(label = domain),
    size = 3.5,
    box.padding = 0.5,
    max.overlaps = 20
  ) +
  
  # 5. Define a clean color gradient for the standard deviation
  scale_color_viridis_c(
    option = "plasma", 
    name = "Ideological Dispersion (SD)\nLow = Exclusive/Echo Chamber\nHigh = Cross-Partisan"
  ) +
  
  # 6. Labels and theme
  labs(
    title = "Media Domain Mapping: Ideology, Frequency, and Dispersion",
    x = "Ideological Center of Gravity (Left < 0 > Right)",
    y = "Total Shares (Log10 Scale)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# STEP 1: Baseline Ideology Check (Wolves vs. Rest)
# ==============================================================================
cat("--- T-Test: Baseline Ideology of Wolves vs Non-Wolves ---\n")
ideology_ttest <- t.test(ideology_2021 ~ is_wolf, data = nodes_breakdown)
print(ideology_ttest)

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 2: Classify Domains
# ==============================================================================
# Determine the 75th percentile of standard deviation to define "Universal"
sd_threshold <- quantile(domain_ideology_summary$weighted_sd_ideology, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)

classified_domains <- domain_ideology_summary %>%
  mutate(
    domain_category = case_when(
      weighted_sd_ideology >= sd_threshold ~ "Universal",
      weighted_mean_ideology <= -0.5 ~ "Far-Left",
      weighted_mean_ideology > -0.5 & weighted_mean_ideology <= -0.1 ~ "Left",
      weighted_mean_ideology > -0.1 & weighted_mean_ideology < 0.1 ~ "Center",
      weighted_mean_ideology >= 0.1 & weighted_mean_ideology < 0.5 ~ "Right",
      weighted_mean_ideology >= 0.5 ~ "Far-Right",
      TRUE ~ "Unclassified" # Catch-all for safety
    )
  )

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 3: Calculate Author-Level Proportions
# ==============================================================================
author_domain_stats <- domain_long %>%
  # Join the classified domains back to the raw sharing data
  inner_join(classified_domains %>% select(domain, domain_category), by = "domain") %>%
  
  # Calculate total shares and categorical shares per author
  group_by(author) %>%
  mutate(total_author_shares = sum(share_count, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  group_by(author, domain_category, total_author_shares) %>%
  summarise(category_shares = sum(share_count, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  
  # Pivot wider to get columns for each category's proportion
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = domain_category, 
    values_from = category_shares, 
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  
  # Calculate the proportion of shares that are Far-Right
  # (Modify this line if you want to test other categories)
  mutate(
    prop_far_right = `Far-Right` / total_author_shares
  ) %>%
  
  # Join back to nodes_breakdown to get the 'is_wolf' and 'ideology_2021' variables
  inner_join(nodes_breakdown %>% select(author, is_wolf, ideology_2021), by = "author")

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 4: Statistical Test (Regression)
# ==============================================================================
# We use OLS regression to test the 'wolf' effect while CONTROLLING for baseline ideology.
# Dependent Variable: Proportion of an author's shares that go to Far-Right domains.

cat("\n--- OLS Regression: Predicting Far-Right Domain Sharing ---\n")
model_far_right <- lm(prop_far_right ~ is_wolf + ideology_2021, data = author_domain_stats)
summary(model_far_right)
```


```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# STEP 1: Isolate the Right-Wing Parliamentarians
# ==============================================================================
# Filter for legislators with an ideology score > 0
right_nodes <- nodes_breakdown %>% 
  filter(ideology_2021 > 0)

# Join their sharing behavior with the previously calculated domain metrics
right_shares <- domain_long %>%
  inner_join(right_nodes %>% select(author, is_wolf, ideology_2021), by = "author") %>%
  inner_join(domain_ideology_summary, by = "domain")

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 2: Extract the Top 20 Domains (Wolves vs. Non-Wolves)
# ==============================================================================
cat("--- Top 20 Domains Shared by Right-Wing WOLVES ---\n")
top_wolf_domains <- right_shares %>%
  filter(is_wolf == 1) %>%
  group_by(domain) %>%
  summarise(
    total_wolf_shares = sum(share_count),
    domain_mean_ideology = first(weighted_mean_ideology),
    domain_exclusivity_sd = first(weighted_sd_ideology),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = total_wolf_shares, n = 20)
print(top_wolf_domains)

cat("\n--- Top 20 Domains Shared by Right-Wing NON-WOLVES ---\n")
top_nonwolf_domains <- right_shares %>%
  filter(is_wolf == 0) %>%
  group_by(domain) %>%
  summarise(
    total_nonwolf_shares = sum(share_count),
    domain_mean_ideology = first(weighted_mean_ideology),
    domain_exclusivity_sd = first(weighted_sd_ideology),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = total_nonwolf_shares, n = 20)
print(top_nonwolf_domains)

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 3: Aggregate Author-Level Metrics for Statistical Testing
# ==============================================================================
author_right_stats <- right_shares %>%
  group_by(author, is_wolf, ideology_2021) %>%
  summarise(
    total_author_shares = sum(share_count),
    
    # Calculate the average extremity and exclusivity of the domains this author shares,
    # weighted by how often they share them.
    author_avg_domain_extremity = sum(share_count * weighted_mean_ideology) / total_author_shares,
    author_avg_domain_exclusivity = sum(share_count * weighted_sd_ideology) / total_author_shares,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 4: Hypothesis Testing
# ==============================================================================

cat("\n--- Test 1: Do Right-Wing Wolves Share a Higher VOLUME of Links? ---\n")
# Using a regression to control for baseline ideology
vol_model <- lm(total_author_shares ~ is_wolf + ideology_2021, data = author_right_stats)
print(summary(vol_model))

cat("\n--- Test 2: Do Right-Wing Wolves Share More EXTREME (Further Right) Domains? ---\n")
extremity_model <- lm(author_avg_domain_extremity ~ is_wolf + ideology_2021, data = author_right_stats)
print(summary(extremity_model))

cat("\n--- Test 3: Do Right-Wing Wolves Share More EXCLUSIVE (Lower SD) Domains? ---\n")
# Note: A negative coefficient for is_wolf here means they share MORE exclusive domains
exclusivity_model <- lm(author_avg_domain_exclusivity ~ is_wolf + ideology_2021, data = author_right_stats)
print(summary(exclusivity_model))
```

```{r}

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 1: Define the "Hyper-Partisan Right" Echo Chambers
# Thresholds: highly exclusive (SD < 0.15) AND explicitly right-wing (Mean > 0.3)
# This perfectly captures domains like plenonews, mblnews, revistaoeste, etc.
# ==============================================================================
hyper_partisan_domains <- domain_ideology_summary %>%
  mutate(
    is_hyper_partisan_right = if_else(
      weighted_sd_ideology < 0.15 & weighted_mean_ideology > 0.3, 
      1, 
      0
    )
  ) %>%
  select(domain, is_hyper_partisan_right)

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 2: Calculate the "Alternative Share" per Right-Wing Author
# We calculate the ratio of hyper-partisan shares to total shares, isolating 
# the concentration of their echo-chamber footprint.
# ==============================================================================
author_alt_media_stats <- right_shares %>%
  # Join the hyper-partisan classification to the right-wing sharing data
  left_join(hyper_partisan_domains, by = "domain") %>%
  
  # Group by author and their attributes to calculate the required metrics
  group_by(author, is_wolf, ideology_2021) %>%
  summarise(
    total_shares = sum(share_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    hyper_partisan_shares = sum(share_count * is_hyper_partisan_right, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    # Calculate the dependent variable: Proportion of media diet that is hyper-partisan
    prop_hyper_partisan = hyper_partisan_shares / total_shares,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 3: The Crucial Statistical Test (Within-Group Comparison)
# Does being a "wolf" predict a higher concentration of hyper-partisan media, 
# holding constant their baseline conservative ideology?
# ==============================================================================
cat("--- OLS Regression: Predicting Hyper-Partisan Media Concentration (Right-Wing Only) ---\n")
alt_media_model <- lm(prop_hyper_partisan ~ is_wolf + ideology_2021, data = author_alt_media_stats)
print(summary(alt_media_model))

# Optional: View the top authors with the highest concentration of hyper-partisan domains
cat("\n--- Top 10 Right-Wing Authors by Hyper-Partisan Share ---\n")
author_alt_media_stats %>%
  arrange(desc(prop_hyper_partisan)) %>%
  select(author, is_wolf, prop_hyper_partisan, total_shares) %>%
  head(10) %>%
  print()
```



```{r}

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 1: Define the Competing Media Factions
# ==============================================================================
# We define the two flagship clusters based on the descriptive Top 20 lists
wolf_flagships <- c("plenonews", "revistaoeste", "conexaopolitica", "renovamidia", "gazetabrasil")
nonwolf_flagships <- c("mblnews") # Kim Kataguiri's primary vehicle

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 2: Calculate Factional Loyalty per Author
# ==============================================================================
intra_right_split <- right_shares %>%
  group_by(author, is_wolf) %>%
  summarise(
    total_wolf_media = sum(share_count[domain %in% wolf_flagships], na.rm = TRUE),
    total_mbl_media = sum(share_count[domain %in% nonwolf_flagships], na.rm = TRUE),
    total_overall_shares = sum(share_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Filter out legislators who don't engage in either alternative ecosystem 
  # (to focus specifically on those consuming hyper-partisan media)
  filter(total_wolf_media > 0 | total_mbl_media > 0) %>%
  
  # Calculate normalized proportions to see their "diet composition"
  mutate(
    prop_wolf_media = total_wolf_media / (total_wolf_media + total_mbl_media),
    wolf_status = ifelse(is_wolf == 1, "Wolf (Bolsonarista)", "Non-Wolf (Institutional/MBL)")
  )

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 3: Statistical Check (Correlation of Factional Media)
# ==============================================================================
cat("--- Pearson Correlation: Sharing Wolf Media vs. Sharing MBL Media ---\n")
# If the right is fractured, this correlation will be near zero or negative.
cor_test <- cor.test(intra_right_split$total_wolf_media, intra_right_split$total_mbl_media)
print(cor_test)

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 4: The Visualization (The Bimodal Scatter Plot)
# ==============================================================================
ggplot(intra_right_split, aes(x = total_mbl_media, y = total_wolf_media)) +
  
  # Plot points, sized by overall share volume, colored by actual Wolf classification
  geom_point(aes(color = wolf_status, size = total_overall_shares), alpha = 0.7) +
  
  # Log10 scales are critical here because Kataguiri's volume will compress the rest of the graph
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
  
  # Add labels for the most extreme outliers (like Kim Kataguiri and top wolves)
  geom_text_repel(
    data = intra_right_split %>% filter(total_wolf_media > 100 | total_mbl_media > 100),
    aes(label = author),
    size = 3.5,
    box.padding = 0.5,
    max.overlaps = 15
  ) +
  
  # Aesthetic styling
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Wolf (Bolsonarista)" = "darkred", "Non-Wolf (Institutional/MBL)" = "steelblue")) +
  labs(
    title = "The Fractured Right: Competing Alternative Media Ecosystems",
    subtitle = "Authors align almost exclusively with either MBL News or the Bolsonarista cluster",
    x = "Total Shares of MBL News (Log10)",
    y = "Total Shares of Wolf Ecosystem Domains (Log10)",
    color = "Legislator Classification",
    size = "Total Output (All Domains)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
```


```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(forcats)

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 1: Calculate Group-Level Shares
# (You can use 'domain_long' to compare against the entire parliament, 
# or 'right_shares' to compare strictly within the right. Using right_shares here.)
# ==============================================================================
group_shares <- right_shares %>%
  group_by(is_wolf, domain) %>%
  summarise(shares = sum(share_count, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 2: Calculate Log Odds Ratio for Every Domain
# ==============================================================================
domain_signatures <- group_shares %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = is_wolf, 
    values_from = shares, 
    values_fill = 0, 
    names_prefix = "wolf_"
  ) %>%
  rename(non_wolf_shares = wolf_0, wolf_shares = wolf_1) %>%
  mutate(
    # Total shares per group across all domains
    total_non_wolf = sum(non_wolf_shares),
    total_wolf = sum(wolf_shares),
    
    # Calculate rates with +1 pseudo-count (Laplace smoothing)
    rate_non_wolf = (non_wolf_shares + 1) / (total_non_wolf + 1),
    rate_wolf = (wolf_shares + 1) / (total_wolf + 1),
    
    # Calculate Log Odds Ratio
    log_odds_ratio = log(rate_wolf / rate_non_wolf),
    
    # Total volume for filtering
    total_shares = wolf_shares + non_wolf_shares
  ) %>%
  # Filter out low-N noise (e.g., a domain shared twice by a wolf shouldn't be deemed "highly distinctive")
  filter(total_shares >= 20)

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 3: Extract the Most Distinctive Domains for Both Factions
# ==============================================================================
top_distinctive <- domain_signatures %>%
  group_by(log_odds_ratio > 0) %>%
  slice_max(abs(log_odds_ratio), n = 15) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    # Assign a label for the plot
    faction = ifelse(log_odds_ratio > 0, "Distinctly Wolf", "Distinctly Non-Wolf"),
    # Order domains by their log odds ratio for clean plotting
    domain = fct_reorder(domain, log_odds_ratio)
  )

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 4: Visualize the Differential Signatures
# ==============================================================================
ggplot(top_distinctive, aes(x = log_odds_ratio, y = domain, fill = faction)) +
  geom_col(alpha = 0.8) +
  
  # Add text showing the actual share counts (Wolf / Non-Wolf)
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = paste0(wolf_shares, " / ", non_wolf_shares),
      hjust = ifelse(log_odds_ratio > 0, -0.1, 1.1)
    ),
    size = 3
  ) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Distinctly Wolf" = "darkred", "Distinctly Non-Wolf" = "steelblue")) +
  
  # Expand X limits slightly to ensure the text labels aren't cut off
  expand_limits(x = c(min(top_distinctive$log_odds_ratio) * 1.2, max(top_distinctive$log_odds_ratio) * 1.2)) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Differential Media Signatures: Wolves vs. Non-Wolves",
    subtitle = "Log Odds Ratio of domain sharing. Labels show absolute shares (Wolf / Non-Wolf).",
    x = "Log Odds Ratio (< 0: Non-Wolf | > 0: Wolf)",
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Faction Signature"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  )
```
